title: Currency formatting contract says currency is required but silently defaults to EUR

evidence.quote: currency?: string; // e.g. 'EUR' — required when style is 'currency'

reasoning: The public type marks currency optional while the comment says it is required for currency style, and the implementation silently substitutes EUR. For linked financial values, an omitted currency code can produce a plausible but wrong document value instead of a type error or runtime error.
reproduction: formatValue('1200', { style: 'currency', locale: 'en-US' }) returns an EUR-formatted value even though the caller did not choose EUR.
recommendation: Either make the type a discriminated union requiring currency for style:'currency' or update the documented contract to state EUR is the default. If correctness matters for financial links, prefer requiring the currency explicitly.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Currency tests always pass a currency code and do not exercise the missing-currency branch.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a formatValue test for style:'currency' without currency that asserts the chosen contract, either a thrown error/type-level fixture or an explicit EUR default.
minimumFixScope: packages/core/src/links/format.ts type/API contract and links.test coverage.
